classification.difficultyReason: Students apply the taught auxiliary-parallel construction at two bends, derive a symbolic difference for the middle segment, and combine it with the supplement of gamma. Keeping the angle orientations consistent is the main demand.

spec.description: Two horizontal parallel lines with matching right-pointing marks and a three-segment bent transversal. The first bend has x in the obtuse region above and to its right; gamma is below the upper parallel, alpha is inside the rightmost vertex, and beta is above the lower parallel.
spec.mathematics: The marked obtuse angle satisfies x = 180 degrees - gamma + alpha - beta.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the source givens and unknown are visible.

answer.short:
$x=180^\circ-\gamma+\alpha-\beta$.

Draw parallels through the bends and use alternate angles and a straight angle.
answer.worked:
Draw horizontal lines through both bends, parallel to the given lines. Let $\theta$ be the acute angle between the middle segment and a horizontal line. At the rightmost vertex, alternate angles give
$$\begin{align*}\theta+\beta&=\alpha\\\theta&=\alpha-\beta.\end{align*}$$
At the first bend, the upper-left segment makes an angle $180^\circ-\gamma$ with the horizontal ray to the right. Therefore
$$\begin{align*}x&=180^\circ-\gamma+\theta\\x&=180^\circ-\gamma+\alpha-\beta.\end{align*}$$
